CHIEF COMPLAINT
Patient wants to quit smoking and has been having difficulty with it.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
44-year-old male presenting for smoking cessation. Patient started smoking in high school, initially experimenting with friends and at parties, which gradually became more regular. He currently smokes daily, approximately a pack and a half per day. He smokes his first cigarette within an hour of waking up. Patient has previously attempted to quit using cold turkey method and was successful for almost a year before relapsing due to work-related stress, including layoffs and increased responsibilities. Patient is highly motivated to quit at this time because he is about to become a father, expecting a daughter any day. He has started meditation and recently joined the gym as stress management strategies. Patient is considering using a nicotine patch for smoking cessation based on friends' success with this method. Planned quit date is next Monday, which is his birthday.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Not discussed.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Type 2 diabetes
History of gout
Systolic murmur (noted on prior examination)

MEDICATIONS
Allopurinol

ALLERGIES
Not discussed.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not discussed.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Smoking: Started in high school. Currently smokes 1.5 packs daily. First cigarette within 1 hour of waking. Previous quit attempt lasted almost 1 year before relapse due to work stress. Recently started meditation and joined gym for stress management. Expecting daughter any day. Employed with increased work responsibilities.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Vitals: Blood pressure 128/88 mmHg, heart rate 68 bpm, respirations 16/min, oxygen saturation 98% on room air.
Cardiac: Regular rate and rhythm. 2/6 systolic murmur appreciated (previously noted, continue monitoring).
Pulmonary: Lungs clear and equal bilaterally. No expiratory wheezes. No rales or rhonchi.
Neck: No lymphadenopathy. No carotid bruits.

RESULTS
Hemoglobin A1c ordered for next blood draw.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. Nicotine dependence: Start 21 mg nicotine patch on Monday (quit date). Gradually decrease dosage over time with no rigid timeline. Change patch location daily to reduce skin irritation. Patient provided handouts on common smoking triggers. Counseled to monitor stress levels related to work and upcoming birth of child. Continue exercise routine and meditation; consider adding yoga. Follow-up in 2 weeks to reassess and reevaluate nicotine patch dosage.

2. Type 2 diabetes: Continue management with diet and exercise. Monitor with hemoglobin A1c to be checked at next blood draw; results to be reviewed at follow-up.

3. History of gout: Continue allopurinol. Continue monitoring dietary factors that exacerbate uric acid levels.

4. Systolic murmur: Continue to monitor.
